title: Uniform Sampling of Proper Graph Colorings via Soft Coloring and Partial Rejection Sampling — correctness of the hybrid sampler
author: Sarat Moka, Ava Vahedi
work: Uniform Sampling of Proper Graph Colorings via Soft Coloring and Partial Rejection Sampling
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Theorem 3 (source0.tex lines 466--468, source label thm:hybrid_correct), the correctness of the paper's hybrid sampler: if the exact sampler used on each component produces a uniform proper k-colouring of that component, independently of the configuration outside it, then the hybrid gamma-PRS algorithm halts in finite time almost surely and outputs a uniformly selected proper colouring. The complete original proof is delivered at source0.tex lines 469--483 (15 adjacent lines). The theorem is the correctness half of the paper's main algorithmic contribution (uniform sampling of proper graph colourings by soft colouring and partial rejection sampling): the proof analyses the distribution at the end of the inner while loop, proves it is supported on the admissible set and uniform there, establishes almost sure halting through the acceptance probability of the partial-rejection step, and identifies the output law as the uniform law on proper colourings. H2: a complete original research-paper correctness theorem whose proof is a genuine distributional argument rather than a routine verification.
